code_findings.title: For ChatGoogle.ainvoke calls with any non-None thinking_budget, including an explicitly requested positive fixed budget, the method sends -1 instead of the configured value. The evidence does not esta
code_findings.explanation: The public field accepts an integer or None, but ainvoke tests only for None and then hard-codes -1. The resulting config is passed directly to generate_content. Therefore, for an explicit positive value such as 100, the transmitted thinking_budget is deterministically -1 rather than 100. The changed line replaces the prior use of self.thinking_budget and introduces this behavior. No in-repository callers were found, and Google's meanings for 0 and -1 are absent, so the stronger disable-versus-dynamic semantic claim is not confirmed.
code_findings.impact: Caused by the change: The change replaced {'thinking_budget': self.thinking_budget} with {'thinking_budget': -1}. Consequently, every non-None configured value takes the branch at line 201, is replaced by -1 at line 202, and is sent in the API config at line 220; an explicitly requested positive fixed budget is therefore not transmitted.

pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: The Google chat adapter expands its declared Gemini model set, changes thinking configuration sent to Google, delegates retries to the Google client, improves native structured-response parsing, and adds timing/error diagnostics.

behavior_changes.description: The adapter's declared model choices now include Gemini 2.5 Flash, Flash Lite, and Pro identifiers, allowing typed callers to select those names.
evidence: Three Gemini 2.5 identifiers were added to the Literal model declaration.

behavior_changes.description: Thinking configuration is now included by default, and every non-None thinking_budget value results in an outbound thinking_budget of -1 rather than the caller-supplied value.
evidence: The field default changed from None to 0.
Request construction tests only for non-None and assigns the constant -1.

behavior_changes.description: ChatGoogle no longer performs its own pattern-based, ten-attempt retry loop around generation; it invokes the request once at this layer and relies on retry behavior provided by the Google client.
evidence: The manual retry loop and exponential backoff were removed.
The replacement explicitly delegates retries and directly awaits one helper invocation.

citations.quoted_text: # Let Google client handle retries internally with proper connection management

behavior_changes.description: When native structured output has no parsed object but does contain text, JSON enclosed by complete Markdown code fences is now unwrapped before JSON decoding and model validation.
evidence: The native structured-output path strips ```json or generic ``` wrappers before calling json.loads.

behavior_changes.description: Google generation calls now produce model-specific debug timing logs and explicit warning/error diagnostics for empty responses and failed calls.
evidence: The invocation records start time, elapsed completion time, empty text, and exceptions.

important_symbols.reason: This contains the request configuration, external asynchronous generation call, structured-output handling, retry delegation, and error translation; nearly all observable behavior changes occur here.
This defines the model identifiers presented as valid to typed callers and now includes three Gemini 2.5 variants.
This introduces the per-model observability boundary used for timing, response, parsing, and failure diagnostics.

investigation_hints.description: Trace construction and invocation of ChatGoogle to determine which workflows provide thinking_budget, model names, and structured output formats.
Inspect Google client creation and SDK configuration to establish the effective retry, timeout, cancellation, and connection-management policy after removal of the local retry loop.

local_risks.description: Caller-provided thinking budgets are ignored: any non-None value, including the new default of 0, is converted to -1. If callers rely on a fixed or disabled thinking budget, requests will not enforce their configured value.

The special diagnostic branch for asyncio.CancelledError appears unreachable through the surrounding except Exception handler on Python versions where CancelledError derives directly from BaseException. Actual task cancellation may therefore bypass the new status/message conversion.
